title: Young versus older audiences for jazz in France
summary: Only the young listened in France, as a fashion; with Bechet gone, rock and roll and the twist took over, and New Orleans jazz fans are often foreigners.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I, uh... You finished? I think so. There are some things I wasn't sure if you discussed there. And, uh... Did you explain the difference between the young audiences and the old audiences? And, uh, the amount of interest, how intensely they're interested?

No. Not exactly. Uh... In France, uh... I think that the... The people of a certain age, they don't care about jazz. It's only the young. But the people of 40, 50, 60, or 60, don't care about jazz. Not like here, because I saw, here at the Fashion Hall, a lot of people of 40 or 50 years. In France, not at all. It's only the young. Mm-hm. by the modes. So, it was 10 years ago, it was the mode of the Jazz New Orleans. Bechet was at the mode, we were listening to Bechet and we were listening to Bechet. Now Bechet is dead, the rock and roll and the twist are coming, and now we are listening to the rock and roll and the twist. And the few of the people who listen to the Jazz New Orleans at Paris are often from the Irish, the Germans, the Italians, the Anglers, many English, but rarely French. Or, it's the young people who are here a little by chance, maybe because they knew someone in the orchestra, because they were more sentimentally, because they had a different culture. But the young people in general, the mass, the majority of the young people, they were interested in the music, well, yeah, yeah, like we used to play in France, that's-to-dire the Johnny Hallyday, and other Beatles, Animals, Surf, and things like that.
